expectations.text: Recommends keeping calculatePrice as its own file (rejects inlining it into the component)
expectations.evidence: Title 'Don't inline it. Keep `calculatePrice.ts` as is.' and 'Keep `pricing/calculatePrice.ts` and its test exactly where they are.'

expectations.text: Grounds it in the abstraction-over-file-structure heuristic (clean typed interface, hides implementation)
expectations.evidence: 'It's fully typed at the boundary. Inputs and outputs are explicit contracts.' and 'This is the opposite of a needless abstraction; it's a clean seam that's earning its keep.'

expectations.text: Notes the agent uses the typed call site without needing the internals (understood in isolation)
expectations.evidence: 'When an agent edits checkout, calculatePrice(...) is right there in the code. Go-to-definition, grep, and the import statement all point straight to the file.' plus the typed boundary framed as the contract; agent works without reading internals.

expectations.text: Rejects the 'inline so Claude sees it all' argument for a clean, reused, tested abstraction
expectations.evidence: 'The AI argument is backwards. The teammate's premise is "Claude sees the whole pricing flow in one place"... But a separate, well-named file is better for AI assistants, not worse.'
